properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 12/19/2025 to XTO ENERGY INC in Center Township, Indiana county. 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect  brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: XTO ENERGY INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/19/2025
Violation Code: 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
Violation ID: 8259399
Permit API: 063-37496
Unconventional: Yes
County: Indiana
Municipality: Center Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/19/2025
Comments: On 12/18/2025, Tim Sands reported a production fluid release from the Fabian Unit A3H well (063-37496). The spill was estimated to be greater than 5 gallons. Today (12/19/2025), I made a site visit. I met Rich Lightner onsite. The Fabian Well Pad had a rig onsite because XTO suspected that there was a hole in the tubing. As they pulled pipe, there was a production fluid release. The estimated release volume was 3.5 barrels (147 gallons). The incident happened at 11:00 am on 12/18/2025 and lasted approximately 9 minutes. XTO believes the release occurred due to a salt block. As the salt blocked dissolved, production fluid and gas was released from the piping. The spill area was isolated to the ground near the rig. No production fluid was discharged from the well pad.XTO marked the release area with flags and had a vacuum truck remove the production fluid from the ground on 12/18/2025. Overnight, it rained. There are now pools of water on the well pad.Due to the spill being greater than 42 gallons, the Department is requesting remediation and attainment of an Act 2 standard. Tipping receipts and waste manifests are requested by the Department associated with removal and disposal of contaminated soil from this spill.As I was leaving the well site, Melissa Breitenbach and Tim Sands called. XTO already contacted Moody and Associates about the cleanup. XTO plans on removing the rig from the site on Monday, 12/29/2025. Then, excavation and remediation will start the week of 1/5/2025. XTO will monitor the site and vacuum pooled water as needed. Violations are noted below.

Comments: On October 3, 2022, the Department conducted an inspection on the Schimizzi S and M 1 well site in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County. Present were myself and WQS Samuel Steingrabe. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3343707 where violations were outstanding due to deteriorated production fluid tanks that were discharging onto the ground, a missing Act 9 sign and Emergency Response plans. Also, no production reports have been submitted since 2014 per Department database. The following was observed:No Act 9 sign was present at the well site entrance (see photos 2 and 3). No Emergency Response plans, or other required postings were onsite. The production fluid tanks onsite appear to have been replaced since IR 3343707 (see photos 5 and 15). Soil conductivity readings were taken underneath and around these tanks to determine whether petroleum products and/or production fluids were still present in the soil since IR 3343707. These readings were taken underneath the production fluid tank valves and in bare spots in their surrounding earthen berms. An additional reading was taken in a wet spot next to the tank farthest from the site entrance. The reading taken underneath the valve of the tank closest to the site entrance read 100 Micro Siemens (see photo 6). The one taken in the surrounding berm read 111 Micro Siemens (see photo 7). The soil conductivity reading taken underneath the valve of the tank farthest from the site entrance read 380 Micro Siemens (see photo 9). The one taken in a bare spot in the surrounding earthen berm read 640 Micro Siemens (see photo 11). The additional reading taken in the wet spot adjacent to the brine tank read 390 Micro Siemens (see photo 8). A background conductivity reading was taken in a well-vegetated spot at the well site entrance, reading 250 Micro Siemens see photo 16). No well tag was observed on the well or associated equipment with correct information (see photo 13), and the well API number was written on the meter box with sharpie. Additional piping and production equipment was left onsite (see photo 10). Some tire rutting was observed at the back of the well site looking from the road, which could be due to third party traversing (see photo 14). The ground overall was soft, which could lead to future stabilization concerns. Therefore, the Department recommends that the operator take additional stabilization measures to prevent any potential E and S issues from developing. Based on observations from today's inspection, the impacted soil appears to have been removed as of October 3, 2022 and violations against the production fluid tanks have been corrected. However, outstanding violations that were continued in IR 3343707 due to production fluid discharge on the ground shall remain open since no NOV response or any information requested has been received from the operator to evaluate whether the release was remediated in accordance with chapter 78a. All other violations shall remain open as well since the rest of the site remains unchanged since IR 3343707.

The one taken in a bare spot in the surrounding earthen berm read 640 Micro Siemens (see photo 11). The additional reading taken in the wet spot adjacent to the brine tank read 390 Micro Siemens (see photo 8). A background conductivity reading was taken in a well-vegetated spot at the well site entrance, reading 250 Micro Siemens see photo 16). No well tag was observed on the well or associated equipment with correct information (see photo 13), and the well API number was written on the meter box with sharpie. Additional piping and production equipment was left onsite (see photo 10). Some tire rutting was observed at the back of the well site looking from the road, which could be due to third party traversing (see photo 14). The ground overall was soft, which could lead to future stabilization concerns. Therefore, the Department recommends that the operator take additional stabilization measures to prevent any potential E and S issues from developing. Based on observations from today's inspection, the impacted soil appears to have been removed as of October 3, 2022 and violations against the production fluid tanks have been corrected. However, outstanding violations that were continued in IR 3343707 due to production fluid discharge on the ground shall remain open since no NOV response or any information requested has been received from the operator to evaluate whether the release was remediated in accordance with chapter 78a. properties.content:
Report Details

Comments: On 11/21/2024, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/alterations inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. It was 36 degrees and partly cloudy when I arrived on location. Rainfall had impacted the region in the past 24 hours.Inspecting the original Taft 851 1V pad, I did witness a secondary containment structure containing drilling mats with water at the level of the containment wall and fluid from the containment on the unprotected ground (picture 5). The water field tested at 0.301 mS conductance. Seneca's Jeff Passerrello was notified and was scheduling to have the containment emptied.Anthony Murphy described current operations as follows: A Nextier frac fleet has finished completion operations on five new wells at the site. Two snubbing/well servicing units were on site, drilling plugs out of the five completed wells. The units were on the first two wells and Anthony expects it to take a week to drill plugs on each well. He expects the crews to finish drilling plugs on all five wells by 12/10/2024. Anthony accompanied me on the site inspection. All operations were being conducted within a plastic lined containment structure that was protected by drilling mats. I did witness frac tanks, gas buster tanks, vac boxes and various chemical totes staged in secondary containment. There were ten frac tanks with fresh and produced water, six gas busters, and eight vac boxes staged near the snubbing/servicing units all staged in secondary containment. 28 frac tanks were staged in secondary containment on the west side of the location. I did witness water in the transfer manifold duck pond on the west side of the snubbing units that field tested at 19.99 mS conductance. Anthony will have the liquids removed.During the inspection, I did witness a 5' x 8' water puddle near the north-central pad outfall that field tested at 19.99 mS conductance; I collected water sample 9551-145. The upper conductivity limit of the Oakton PCTS5 is 19.99 mS. Water discharging from the north-central pad outfall into the sediment basin field tested at 19.99 mS conductance; I collected water sample 9551-146 and soil sample 9551-147. Water in the basin near the northeast overflow field tested at 3.07 mS conductance; I collected water sample 9551-148. Vegetation is established in recently constructed areas. Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Infiltration berm 3 and the sedimentation basin did have standing water. Temporary compost filter socks remain installed throughout the site. Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations. As recommended in the inspections listed above, the DEP continues to recommend pursuing Act 2 for the large amount of elevated conductance fluids discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin.The DEP recommends the following: 1. Remove the elevated conductance fluids and contaminated soils from the pad surface and the sediment basin.2. Continuously monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered.3. Monitor secondary containment structures for contaminants, for liquid levels and for adequate freeboard levels; remove liquids as necessary.I left the site at 1300 hours.

Comments: On 1/27/19 at 0945 hrs., I conducted an inspection in response to a crude oil release that was reported to the Department on 1/25/20, and initially was discovered on 1/24/20. The release occurred near Howard Drilling, Inc.'s TLC 1 well (API 063-32818) in Conemaugh Twp., Indiana Co. According to initial reports, and verified by Mr. Dale "Wally" Howard via telephone on 1/27/20, approximately 80 barrels of crude oil was transferred from stock tanks at two nearby wells (063-22666 and 063-31878) during plugging operations, to two 100 barrel holding tanks located adjacent to Hogue Drive. According to Mr. Howard, the holding tanks belong to Tunnelton Liquids Company (property owner). ARG Refining was scheduled to pick the oil up on 1/24/20. The driver notified Howard Drilling on 1/24/20 that the tanks were empty. The driver then walked over to the release area and confirmed that crude oil had been released from the tanks, but was uncertain of he extent of the release. Mr. Howard had crews onsite on 1/24/20 and notified the Department of the release on 1/25/20. According to Mr. Howard, the driver reported that the valve to the tanks was open and a hose was connected to the tank valve and led to a drain in the adjacent cement pad. The crude oil flowed through the drain, under Hogue Drive and around a concrete secondary containment structure. The oil then flowed South through an old mine drainage treatment pond, and into a canal, which drains to the Conemaugh. McCutcheon Enterprises was contracted by Howard Drilling on 1/25/20 to begin the cleanup process. During my inspection, McCutcheon was in the process of excavating surface soils. In addition to the excavation, McCutcheon was also going to replace the underflow dam with one made of sand-filled super sacs. There was concern that the original dam was constructed with contaminated soil and this material was to be removed. McCutcheon was also conducting boom maintenance along the spill path. During my inspection, it was evident that some residual crude material remained in the drainage canal south of the release site; however, had still not made it to the down-gradient culvert leading to the Conemaugh River. The release of crude oil onto the ground and into waters of the Commonwealth constitutes violations of CSL 301, CSL 307(a), 78.57(a), SWMA 301, SWMA 302(A), and SWMA 610(1). Failure to immediately notify the Department of the release constitutes violations of 91.33(A) and 78.66(a). These violations have been closed as "unresolvable". Failure to have adequate secondary containment around the tanks constitutes a violation of 78.64(a). The existing containment structure was backfilled and did not have sufficient capacity to prevent the release from impacting waters of the Commonwealth. This constitutes a violation of 78.64(b). You are hereby requested to follow Department Policy 800-5000-001, Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil & Gas Well Sites or Access Roads. This Policy sets forth he procedures that should be followed to resolve the violations associated with the release noted in this Notice of Violation by using either the Act 2 or Alternative Remediation Process. A copy of the Policy is attached for your review.

Comments: This conventional well is equipped to produce with a pump jack, a site ID sign is posted on the jack. There are no surface concerns evident on the well site at this time. 2025 APR and MIA information were submitted for this well.The tank battery for Trinity Mineral Partners' Roell lease is located approximately 500 feet to the west of this well, and is accessed off of Rounds Hill Road.This tank battery consists of two earthen containments. One containment consists of two 210 bbl stock tanks and separators, there are no surface issues evident at this containment. A second earthen containment (located southwest/downslope of the aforementioned one) holds a horizontal (approximate 250 bbl capacity) steel production water tank. There is an approximate 10' x 200' area that has been recently excavated beyond the end of the spur road that is used to access the tank battery, and continues adjacent to and downslope of, the production water tank/containment and ends at the edge of the bank that runs parallel to Rounds Hill Road. Mulch has been sparsely applied across the excavated area. Deer tracks are prevalent throughout the excavated area downslope of the production water tank/containment.Water is seeping out of the southwest corner of the production water tank containment, the specific conductance (SPC) of this water is elevated (> 1000 uS/cm). The SPC of the material at (and downslope of) the southwest corner of the production water tank containment is also elevated. Elevated SPC continues to be observed in standing water and the soil within the aforementioned excavated area downslope of the production water tank containment. Beyond the excavated area, there is an approximate 50 foot section of stressed vegetation evident on the bank of Rounds Hill Road. The SPC of the soil along this section of road bank is also elevated. The SPC of the Rounds Hill Road ditch water downslope of the aforementioned area of stressed vegetation is approximately ten times higher than the ditch water upslope of this point. The Rounds Hill Road ditch water continues to have elevated SPC for another 200 feet until the ditch enters an unnamed tributary (UNT) of Jackson Run.There was no obvious discharge from the production water tank during this inspection, the prevalence of elevated SPC and stressed vegetation in the material that comprises the containment and areas downslope of the containment is indicative of production water discharges into the containment due to poor housekeeping and/or a lack of tank integrity. The evidence obtained during this inspection also indicates that the containment surrounding the production water tank was not constructed in a manner to prevent the tank contents from reaching waters of this Commonwealth.An SAC 942 water sample was collected from standing water located in the excavated area downslope of the production water tank containment.In addition to the information requested in the attached Notice of Violation, it is requested that Trinity Mineral Partners reveal how the aforementioned excavated soil was disposed and provide any supporting documentation regarding its disposal.

Violation ID: 8215764

Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 1/31/2025
Comments: On January 31, 2025 the Department conducted an Incident inspection of the PF Eisaman South 43 well pad located in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County in response to a spill that reportedly occurred on Monday, January 27, 2025. Accompanying on today's inspection is CNX representative Jessie Valentine. Mr. Valentine showed the Department the area where the spill occurred and stated that the spill occurred due to a piping/equipment failure, and that the release was approximately two barrels of production fluid.At the time of this inspection, Mr. Valentine stated that remediation efforts had occurred, and that fresh gravel has been laid in the spill area. The Department observed a large area between the production tanks and GPUs where new gravel appeared to be laid. The Department took a background soil conductivity reading upslope on the well pad's perimeter (0.0894 mS), and then took several readings in the area where fresh gravel was laid (0.0103 mS, 0.492 mS, 0.0436 mS, 9.68 mS, 6.38 mS, 0.787 mS, and 0.413 mS) to assess if any impacted materials remained on site. These soil conductivity readings when compared to the background soil conductivity reading subjugate that there are still some areas where the spill has not been fully excavated. Mr. Valentine spray painted the areas where the Department took elevated readings at, so they can easily identified for future remediation. The Department recommends the Operator fully remediate the release and dispose of all contaminated material properly and in accordance with regulations. The Department is requesting the Operator submit a written response within 15 days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, plan for further remediation of the spill or release and assessment of any impacts to water of the Commonwealth. The Department is requesting how the Operator quantified the amount spilled and is requesting the Operator follow the Act 2 guidelines as set by 78a.66(c)(2). At the time of this inspection, the Act 9 sign was posted at the access road entrance with all required information posted on it, and inside the on-site mailbox was the Emergency Response Plan (ERP) and Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency (PPC) Plan. The Ac 9 sign had a different Operator than the ERP and PPC Plan, the Department recommends the Operator update all plans as applicable. The access road appeared stabilized with gravel and no erosion or sedimentation issues were observed, and all of the well pad perimeters appeared to be exhibiting at least 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed.At the time of this inspection, the well pad had 6 wells on it on it as well as 3 production tanks within secondary containment and 6 GPUs within secondary containment, at the time of this inspection no active fluid leaks or fluid discharge were observed coming from or near any of this production equipment. The 2H well (SPUD 4/20/2017) had a well tag fixed to it with the API number on it, but this well tag did not have any of the Operator's information on it. The Department is recommending the Operator update the well tag and/or well posting to have all required information posted on it in accordance with 3211(g). While on site, the Department spoke with CNX representative Chad Eisenman via the phone to inform him of the Department's findings during this inspection and verbally requested the aforementioned information.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for an approximately 2 barrel release of production fluid onto the well pad. A subsequent inspection will be conducted to assess further remedial measures. An Act 2 Report has not yet been submitted to the Environmental Cleanup and Brownfields (ECB) Program.

Comments: On May 6, 2025, an inspection was conducted in response to a spill at the A J Stahura 8 well site in Susquehanna Township, Cambria County. This spill was discovered by the operator on the day prior to this inspection, which is suspected by the operator to have been caused by trespassing vandals opening the brine tank valve when operator representatives were not present onsite. The Department spoke with operator representative Will Warfel on 5/05/2025, who stated that the last time operator representatives were onsite was most likely one month prior to detecting this spill, when the chart was changed and the brine tank level was read. Reporting of this spill is covered in IR 3974873. Mr. Warfel was onsite was onsite with the Department during this inspection.The following was observed:Upon arrival, the Department spoke with Mr. Warfel who identified a stream crossing of Kings Run as part of the access road to the well site (see photo 1). He then requested recommendations for dispersing the weight of commercial vehicles that haul the excavation equipment onsite to protect the cross-culverts when they traverse this location (see photo 4). Further review will be conducted by the Department regarding this matter. What appears to be scouring was observed on the upstream side of the stream crossing. A brown foam that appears to be biological in nature was observed at the top of the water in this location (see photo 3). An erosion channel was going down the access road toward the downstream location of the stream crossing (see photos 5 and 6). Mr. Warfel stated that this access road is utilized by additional parties. Further review via Google Earth Historic Imagery suggests that this portion of the access road most likely predates the well site. Additional muddy tire rutting was observed in the rest of the access road going toward the well site (see photos 7 and 8).The well head is equipped with a well tag and appears to be free of fluid leaks at the time of inspection (see photo 10). The operator's information is posted on the brine tank (see photo 11). The body of the brine tank appears to be sound at the time of inspection (see photos 12 and 14). The brine tank valve appears to have been closed, therefore it appears that the release has been ceased (see photo 13). Plastic sheeting was placed on the impacted area within the earthen berm. Distressed vegetation was observed where brine fluids were reported by the operator to have traveled downslope (see photos 15-17). Elevated conductivity was detected in the ground starting approximately 25 feet downslope of the brine tank (see photos 18-25). Mr. Warfel confirmed during this inspection that the operator will conduct remediation in accordance with the requirements of Act 2, and that remediation will start on the day of this inspection with light excavation.Based on observations from this inspection, violations shall be issued from this inspection for releasing production fluids to the surface of the ground. The operator is requested to submit a written response within 15 business days of the spill or release. This response should include an incident report, a timeline, the regulation substance involved, where the spill or release occur, the environmental media affected, any impacts to water supplies, buildings, or utilities, and interim actions planned, initiated, or completed.Any new impacts discovered or identified during interim remedial actions or site characterization should also be reported to the Department within 15 calendar days of discovery.Within 180 days of the spill or release the operator must perform a site characterization to determine the extent and magnitude of the contamination and submit the site characterization report to the undersigned.The operator shall assess impacts to waters of the Commonwealth from the spill or release.

The area around the well is flat aside from the depression around the pump jack that allowed the crude oil to pool around it. Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/23/2021
Comments: A follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess conditions on both pads. DEP Environmental Trainee John Rogers and DEP Geoscientist Sam Louderback accompanied me on this inspection. We met with company man Bill Mitchell upon arriving on Pad B. On Pad B, the sump remains installed where fluid with elevated conductivity (EC) was observed on the pad surface. Fluid is present within the sump approximately two feet below the pad surface. The EC of this fluid is 2.19 mS/cm. No elevated conductivity fluid was observed on or off the pad. In the rock-lined ditch along the northwest edge of the pad, two small puddles of fluid were found which had a petroleum odor and a sheen. I notified the company man of the presence of these puddles before leaving the location. On Pad A, we met with company man Grant Boyd upon arriving on location. He told us that excavation had been done after the previous inspection on the pad near the northeast corner of the well site secondary containment. Multiple puddles were observed in this area during this inspection which had an EC between 3.43 mS/cm and 4.33 mS/cm. An additional puddle was observed along the pad edge within the brush barrier along the side of the pad. This puddle had an EC of 2.09 mS/cm. I took a sample, sample #0718-178, from this puddle and sent it to the state laboratory the same day to be analyzed for SAC 942 plus Li, Br, and Al. I notified the company man of my findings before leaving the location. In a phone call with Rick Hall on the same day at 13:29, I relayed my observations on both pads to Mr. Hall. He said that he would have the puddles investigated and remediated. Violations remain outstanding for the release on Pad B.

Report Details
Inspection Client: APOLLO RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 1/12/2024
Violation Code: 78.88(b)1-4 - OPERATING WELLS - MECHANICAL INTEGRITY OF OPERATING WELLS - Operator failed to meet minimum requirements for inspections to determine compliance with the well construction and operating requirements.
Violation ID: 8171332
Permit API: 021-21026
Unconventional: No
County: Cambria
Municipality: Clearfield Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/12/2024
Comments: Follow up inspection of the County of Cambria Ivory 1 well conducted on 1/12/2024. Arrived on location at 10:03. Violations were issued on 3/23/2022, 9/22/2022, and 5/2/2023 site inspections for the following: OGA3220(A) - Failure to plug an abandoned well. 78.91(a) - Failure to plug an abandoned well. 78.103 - Failure to monitor well granted Inactive Status on an annual basis and submit monitoring reports. 78.104 - Failure to meet the terms of Inactive Status. 78.88(a) - Failure to inspect each well for compliance with requirements. 78.88(b)1-4 - Failure to meet minimum requirements for inspections. 78.88(e) - Failure to submit Mechanical Integrity Report to the Department. OGA3211(G) - Failure to post the permit number and operators info at the well site. OGA3211(H) - Failure to install the permit number on the well upon completion in a permanent manner. This 1/12/2024 follow up inspection found that the well remains in a similar condition as the previous inspections. Violations were not addressed or responded to. Well is not equipped for production. Pumpjack, meter, and electric boxes remain on site. Much of the equipment has been dismantled. Wellhead is no longer tied inline. No permit number or operator ID found on the well. Wellhead and much of the equipment is overgrown with trees/brush. Well status was previously approved as Regulatory Inactive. Regulatory Inactive status expired on 04/20/2020. Operator failed to plug or return the well to active status. Review found no annual integrity monitoring reports submitted to the Department. Annual Production Reports have been submitted with 0 production shown for at least the last five years. All of the above violations remain outstanding.
